'''Hugh Allen Oliver Hill''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sadler |first=Peter J. |date=2023 |title=Hugh Allen Oliver Hill. 23 May 1937 — 30 July 2021 |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2023.0002 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=75|pages=199–217 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2023.0002 |doi-access=free }}</ref> (23 May 1937 – 30 July 2021), usually known as '''Allen Hill''', was Professor, and later Emeritus Professor, of [[Bioinorganic chemistry|Bioinorganic Chemistry]] at the [[University of Oxford]] and Honorary Fellow of [[The Queen's College, Oxford]], and [[Wadham College, Oxford]].<ref name='WhosWho'> {{cite web | url = http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U20152 | title = HILL, Prof. (Hugh) Allen (Oliver) | accessdate = 31 July 2012 | date = 2012 | work = Who's Who 2012 online edition | publisher = A & C Black}}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1990 and was awarded the 2010 [[Royal Medal]] of the Royal Society "for his pioneering work on protein electrochemistry, which revolutionised the diagnostic testing of glucose and many other bioelectrochemical assays.".<ref name='RoyalMedal'> {{cite web | url = http://royalsociety.org/news/excellence-science/ | title = Royal Society recognises excellence in science | accessdate = 31 July 2012 | publisher = Royal Society}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://research.chem.ox.ac.uk/allen-hill.aspx |title=Departmental home page |access-date=31 July 2012 |archive-date=29 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121029224747/http://research.chem.ox.ac.uk/allen-hill.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref>

After studying at [[Queen's University Belfast]]<ref name='WhosWho'/> Hill moved to Oxford in 1962, becoming a fellow of The Queen's College in 1965.<ref name='Debretts'> {{cite web | url = http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/h/16321/%28Hugh%29%20Allen%20Oliver+HILL.aspx | title = Prof Allen Hill, FRS | accessdate = 17 August 2012 | work = Debrett's People of Today Online}}</ref>  His research awards include the Interdisciplinary award, the Chemistry and Electrochemistry of Transition Metals medal, and the Robinson award of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], the Breyer medal of the [[Royal Australian Chemical Institute]] and the [[Mullard Award]] and the Royal Medal of the Royal Society.<ref name='Debretts'/>

In 2012 his work on the [[electrochemical]] monitoring of [[protein]]s and its application to the monitoring of [[glucose]] concentrations in the blood of [[diabetic]] patients was marked by the award of a National Chemical Landmark [[blue plaque]] in Oxford.<ref name='plaque'>{{cite web | url = http://www.rsc.org/AboutUs/News/PressReleases/2012/oxford-university-glucose-sensor-chemical-landmark.asp | title = RSC honours Oxford University team behind diabetic breakthrough | accessdate = 17 August 2012 | last = Gallagher | first = Paul | publisher = [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] | archive-date = 16 October 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121016184951/http://www.rsc.org/AboutUs/News/PressReleases/2012/oxford-university-glucose-sensor-chemical-landmark.asp | url-status = live }}</ref>
